findings.evidence:
`pkg/ddl/multi_schema_change.go:84` calls `w.doAnalyzeWithoutReorg(job, tblInfo)` unconditionally once revertible sub-jobs reach the last revertible point.
`pkg/ddl/index.go:1407` `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg` immediately dereferences `job.ReorgMeta` (`switch job.ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState`) with no nil-guard.
`pkg/ddl/job_worker.go:939` only initializes `job.ReorgMeta` on upgrade when `w.tp` is `addIdxWorker` or `backgroundWorker`.
`pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go:419` dispatches jobs with `reorg=0` to the general worker pool.
`pkg/meta/model/job.go:772` `Job.MayNeedReorg()` can return `false` for `ActionMultiSchemaChange` (so `reorg=0` is possible).
findings.fix:
Add a nil-guard before using `job.ReorgMeta` in the new MSC analyze path, e.g.:
- Initialize in `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`: `if job.ReorgMeta == nil { job.ReorgMeta = &model.DDLReorgMeta{} }`.
- Or initialize in `onMultiSchemaChange` before calling `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`.
- Or broaden the existing upgrade-compat init in `runOneJobStep` to also cover `ActionMultiSchemaChange` even on `generalWorker`.
findings.impact: Compatibility/state-machine risk: an in-flight `ActionMultiSchemaChange` job decoded from an older TiDB version without `reorg_meta` (so `job.ReorgMeta == nil`) can panic when it reaches the new analyze gate. This is most acute when the job is dispatched to the general worker (`reorg=0`), because the existing upgrade-compat initialization does not run there. Result: DDL owner step panic / job stuck / upgrade instability.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09`: `pkg/ddl/multi_schema_change.go` still calls `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg` without a nil-guard; `pkg/ddl/index.go` still dereferences `job.ReorgMeta` in `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`; `pkg/ddl/job_worker.go` still only initializes `ReorgMeta` for `addIdxWorker`/`backgroundWorker`.
findings.verify:
Minimal repro (unit-level): construct a `model.Job{Type: ActionMultiSchemaChange, MultiSchemaInfo: ..., ReorgMeta: nil}` and drive it to the code path where revertible sub-jobs are done; confirm `onMultiSchemaChange` panics at `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`.
Upgrade-level: restore a job record produced by a TiDB build without `reorg_meta` into `mysql.tidb_ddl_job` with `reorg=0`, run the upgraded owner, and observe whether it hits the MSC analyze gate without crashing after applying the nil-guard.
findings.what: Potential nil dereference introduced in the new multi-schema-change embedded-analyze path: `onMultiSchemaChange` now always calls `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`, which assumes `job.ReorgMeta` is non-nil, but upgrade-compat initialization only runs on reorg/background workers; MSC jobs can be dispatched to the general worker (`reorg=0`).

subject: ddl, model: fix unexpected missing analyze for multi schema change (#64337)
summary: Moves DDL analyze for multi-schema-change off sub-jobs (removing non-persisted `NeedAnalyze`) and into the parent MSC job using persisted `ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState`; refactors modify-column temporary naming helpers into `pkg/meta/model` and replaces `CtxVars` with `NeedReorg` for modify-column reorg signaling.
